shards.range: Preface and Introduction through FIR Digital Filter Design
shards.note: Foundations: the book overview, Fourier transforms and practical theorems, spectrum-analysis window families and optimal-window design, and FIR filter design by least-squares, frequency-sampling, window, Hilbert-transform, minimum-phase, and optimal methods.

shards.range: Spectrum Analysis of Sinusoids through Time-Frequency Displays
shards.note: Core analysis: sinusoidal resolution and parameter estimation, noise and power-spectrum estimation, periodograms and Welch analysis, followed by STFT definitions and classic, auditory, and loudness spectrograms.

shards.range: Overlap-Add STFT Processing through Summary and Conclusions
shards.note: Advanced STFT processing: FFT convolution and overlap methods, the uniform filter-bank interpretation, perfect-reconstruction constraints, spectral-modeling and time-scale applications, and multirate/polyphase, MPEG, and wavelet filter banks.

All supporting and advanced material: notation, continuous Fourier theory, statistics, Gaussian properties, perceptual frequency warping, Matlab/Octave examples, spectral-modeling history, the PARSHL program, and complete reference back matter.

notes: The official citation page identifies Julius O. Smith III, W3K Publishing, the 2011 online-book edition, and ISBN 978-0-9745607-3-1. The live Stanford root page returned HTTP 200 and exposes a deeply nested contents tree with 614 distinct linked HTML pages; representative pages from the opening theory, middle STFT material, final PARSHL appendix, bibliography, and index were all directly readable. The current online version is maintained in place (its footer was updated 2026-06-10), so the web text may include corrections beyond the 2011 hardcopy. Four shards were chosen because this is a large book (11 principal technical chapters plus a summary chapter, eight appendices, bibliography, and index), with boundaries placed at major conceptual transitions.
